_README: This file is managed by LazyCue (see shelley/lazycue). Do NOT edit by hand — it is the cached, machine-generated DSL for a self-healing browser test. To change behavior, edit the test description and re-run LazyCue.
description:
The test seeds two conversations: A at /c/catchup-a, whose reply reads "Hello! I'm Shelley, your AI assistant.", and B at /c/catchup-b, whose reply reads "Well, hi there!". A conversation "shows" a text when document.querySelector(".messages-container")?.textContent includes it (wait for that with an eval expecting true, allowing 15s; do not look elsewhere on the page, as the conversation list previews messages too). To "select" a conversation with slug X: click the button[aria-label="Open conversations"]; wait for ".drawer.open" to be visible (allow 5s); wait for the ".drawer.open .conversation-title" whose text is exactly X to be visible (allow 15s) and click it; then wait for ".drawer.open" to be hidden (allow 10s). Perform the steps in order. Only one /api/stream2 EventSource exists, even after switching conversations. Call "stream requests" returns how many requests for /api/stream2 (any query) the browser has sent since the test began, as a number.
1. Navigate to /c/catchup-a; wait for the message input ([data-testid="message-input"]) to be visible (allow 30s); A shows "Hello! I'm Shelley, your AI assistant.".
2. Select catchup-b; it shows "Well, hi there!".
3. Select catchup-a, then select catchup-b, then select catchup-a; it shows "Hello! I'm Shelley, your AI assistant.".
4. Call "stream requests": it must return exactly "1". The stream is held open for the lifetime of the page; switching conversations must not reopen it.
5. performance.getEntriesByType("resource").filter((e) => e.name.includes("/api/stream2")).length must be at most 1 (Resource Timing logs only completed responses, so an open EventSource may show 0).
